what_its_for: Sparsentan is used to slow down kidney damage in adults who have a kidney disease called IgA nephropathy (IgAN), also known as Berger's disease. This condition causes your immune system to deposit harmful proteins in your kidneys, leading to inflammation and scarring over time. Sparsentan helps protect your kidneys by blocking two pathways that cause this damage.
how_to_take: Take sparsentan by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. You must be enrolled in a special safety program called the FILSPARI REMS Program before you can receive this medicine. Your doctor and pharmacist will help set this up for you.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 200 mg taken by mouth once daily. After about 2 weeks, if you are tolerating the medicine well, your doctor will typically increase your dose to 400 mg once daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you respond to treatment and any side effects you experience. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose at the usual time. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store sparsentan at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in a dry place away from moisture and heat. Keep the capsules in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of any leftover medication.
what_to_avoid: Do not take sparsentan if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can cause serious birth defects or loss of the baby. Women who can become pregnant must use two effective forms of birth control during treatment and for 1 month after stopping. Do not drink grapefruit juice or eat grapefruit while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your body and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium unless your doctor approves them, as sparsentan can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid other medicines that lower blood pressure unless your doctor knows about them. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, especially other blood pressure medications or water pills (diuretics).
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: signs of pregnancy (missed period, breast tenderness, nausea); swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (could be a serious allergic reaction); dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting (signs of low blood pressure); sudden decrease in urination or swelling in your legs or ankles (signs of worsening kidney function); muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness (signs of high potassium); yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); or any unusual or severe symptoms that concern you. Your doctor will also regularly check your blood pressure, kidney function, potassium levels, and liver tests while you are on this medicine.
when_it_works: Sparsentan begins working to protect your kidneys right away, but you may not feel any different because kidney disease often has no noticeable symptoms. Studies showed that sparsentan reduced the amount of protein in the urine (a sign of kidney damage) within a few weeks of starting treatment. The long-term benefit of slowing kidney disease progression becomes more apparent over months to years of continued treatment. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor, even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Sparsentan must NOT be used during pregnancy. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. All females who can become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test before starting treatment, use two reliable forms of birth control during treatment, and for 1 month after the last dose. Monthly pregnancy tests are required while on this medicine through the FILSPARI REMS Program. Breastfeeding: It is not known if sparsentan passes into breast milk. Because of the potential risk to a nursing baby, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment and for 1 month after stopping. Older adults (65+): Older patients may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects of this medicine. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver disease, sparsentan may not be safe for you. Your doctor will review your liver health before and during treatment. Children: Sparsentan is not approved for use in patients under 18 years of age.
